Single-player Pong (squash-style). A vertical paddle sits on the left edge, and the right wall is the goal or reward target.

Pong. More precisely, a single-player Pong/squash variant: the agent is a vertical paddle in the left column and returns a ball toward a scoring wall on the right.

Pong, the single-player variant (one paddle against a scoring wall, similar to squash).

A single white ring (circle outline, stroke about 1 px, sometimes 2 px at the bottom) on a black background. The diameter is roughly 5 to 10 pixels. The ring is placed somewhere inside the frame, usually near the centre but shifted up, down, left or right, and it stays at least one pixel away from the image edge. The inside of the ring is black.

- Each image is a single solid white disk (filled circle) on a black background.
- The diameter ranges from about 4 px up to about 9–10 px.
- The disk sits at a varying position, always fully inside the inner 10×10 area. The outermost 1-pixel frame stays black.
- The largest disks are nearly the inscribed circle, touching rows 1 and 10 and columns 1 and 10, but never reaching the corners.

Each image is a single thin (about 1 px) white circle outline, a ring, on a black background.
- Size: diameter about 4–10 px (radius about 2–4.5), most often about 6–8 px.
- Position: the centre is random but always lets the whole ring fit inside rows 1–10 and columns 1–10. The outermost row and column on every side stay black. Small rings can sit in any corner; the largest fill the interior.

Each image is a single thin white circle outline, about 1 pixel wide, on a black background.
- The radius ranges from about 1–1.5 px up to about 4.5 px (diameter roughly 3–10 pixels).
- The centre position varies, but the whole circle always stays inside rows 1–10 and columns 1–10.
- The outer one-pixel frame is always black, and nothing else appears in the image.

One white, 1-pixel-thick rectangle outline per image, on black. Its sides lie anywhere from row/column 1 to row/column 10. Sizes range from small boxes (about 4×4) up to nearly the full 10×10 interior. The inside of the box is black, and the outermost border of the image stays black.

Each image is a single solid white axis-aligned rectangle (sometimes a square) on a black background. It sits inside the 1-pixel black frame, with sides typically 4 to 10 pixels long. Its position and width/height vary independently, so it can be placed off-centre. Most rectangles are fairly large and cover much of the central region.

- Each image is a single solid white axis-aligned rectangle on a black background.
- The rectangle always sits inside the 10×10 interior, so the outermost 1-pixel frame stays black.
- Its position and size vary from image to image. Sides are typically about 3 to 9 pixels, it can touch any side of the interior, and the centre area is covered most often.

Each image is one solid white, axis-aligned filled rectangle on a black background. It always lies inside the central 10×10 area (rows 1–10, columns 1–10), and the 1-pixel outer frame is always black. Position, width and height vary independently. Sizes run from thin bars of 1–2 px up to nearly the whole 10×10 area; typically a side is about 3–8 px, roughly a quarter to a half of the canvas.

Each image is a single hollow, axis-aligned rectangle: a white outline one pixel thick on a black background. Its corners are sharp and its inside is black. Its position and its width and height vary, with sides from about 3 to 10 pixels and typically about 5-8, sometimes near-square. It always lies inside rows 1-10 and columns 1-10, so the outer ring of pixels stays black.

Each image is one solid white, axis-aligned rectangle on a black background. Width and height vary independently, roughly 2–8 pixels and typically 4–6, so many look near-square. The rectangle sits at a random place inside rows 1–10 and columns 1–10. The outer 1-pixel frame is always black, and everything outside the rectangle is black.

A thin white triangle outline on a black background, pointing up.
- The apex is near the top centre (row 1, columns about 5–6).
- Two one-pixel legs slope down to the left and right.
- A horizontal base sits around rows 7–10 and spans up to about columns 1–10.
- The outer border stays black. Size and slopes vary: some triangles are tall and wide, others shorter and narrower.

Each image is a single solid white triangle pointing upward on a black background:
- The apex is near the top centre, around row 1–2 and columns 5–6.
- The sides slope outward by about one column every two rows.
- The flat base sits around rows 8–10 and spans roughly columns 1–10.
- The triangle is typically about 8–9 pixels tall and 8–10 pixels wide.
